summary:
Project Title:
​Earth-Mars Twin Finder (Terrestrial Analog Mapping & Matching Tool)
​Project Summary:
​Selecting future landing sites and permanent bases on the Moon and Mars depends on critical geological, topographical, and environmental factors. While space agencies rely on a few limited terrestrial analogs (such as the Atacama Desert or Death Valley) to test equipment and methods, these sites are not entirely well characterized.  
​Our project proposes an interactive web application powered by open Earth, Moon, and Mars data from NASA and other space agencies. The tool enables researchers and mission planners to match proposed extraterrestrial landing sites with newly identified terrestrial analogs—with a special focus on unexplored desert, volcanic, and arid terrains in the Middle East and North Africa.  
​Key Features:
​Smart Matching Engine: Analyzes parameters like soil composition, slope, and climate to rank matching Earth locations for specific Martian or lunar sites.  
​Risk & Environment Filtering: Categorizes analogs based on mission testing needs, such as rover testing, spacesuit trials, or extreme environment survival.
​Subsurface Habitat Integration: Incorporates data mapping for lava tubes and caves on Earth and planetary bodies to support future subterranean base planning.
details: Build a futuristic NASA JPL mission control web application called 'TERA'. The app should feature a dark aerospace UI using Tailwind CSS, an interactive satellite map preview area, sidebar mission parameter sliders (like rover weight, wheel radius, and slope angle), and real-time calculation charts comparing Egyptian terrestrial analog sites (Gilf Kebir, White Desert, Red Sea Hills) with Mars/Moon planetary counterparts (Jezero Crater, Medusae Fossae, Mare Serenitatis). Make every button, slider, and tab fully functional with clean JavaScript code."
